items.stem: Executives complain the PMO produces many status reports but adds little value. Which change best addresses the root problem?

options.text: Tie PMO metrics to business outcomes and decisions they inform
options.rationale: Correct: linking metrics to outcomes and decisions makes the PMO valuable rather than a report factory.
More of a low-value activity does not add value.

options.text: Add more templates for teams to fill in
options.rationale: Added overhead without outcome linkage does not solve the problem.
Abandoning metrics removes the PMO's ability to show value.

items.explanation: Correct: linking metrics to outcomes and decisions makes the PMO valuable rather than a report factory.

items.stem: A young company with few projects and low process maturity wants a PMO. Which operating model usually fits best initially?

options.text: A supportive PMO providing templates, coaching and light governance
options.rationale: Correct: a supportive model suits low maturity, building capability before heavier control.

options.text: A controlling PMO enforcing strict compliance immediately
options.rationale: Heavy control on immature teams tends to create resistance and overhead.

options.text: A directive PMO that runs every project centrally
options.rationale: Full central control is rarely appropriate for a small, immature portfolio.

options.text: No PMO because the company is small
options.rationale: The scenario establishes the company wants a PMO; the question is the model.

items.explanation: Correct: a supportive model suits low maturity, building capability before heavier control.

items.stem: Designing portfolio prioritisation for the PMO, which TWO practices make selection defensible? (Select TWO)

options.text: Scoring initiatives against explicit, weighted strategic criteria
options.rationale: Correct: transparent weighted criteria make prioritisation defensible.

options.text: Considering capacity and interdependencies, not just individual value
options.rationale: Correct: capacity and dependencies shape what can actually be delivered.

options.text: Ranking strictly by the seniority of the requesting executive
options.rationale: Seniority-based ranking is not a defensible portfolio method.

options.text: Approving every proposed project to avoid conflict
Hiding the criteria so decisions cannot be questioned

items.explanation: Correct: transparent weighted criteria make prioritisation defensible. Correct: capacity and dependencies shape what can actually be delivered.
